# Bazel vs zel code differences: tests

Category rule: `src/test/` unit, integration, shell, Python, native, and test-support sources.

- Failure entries: 1740
- Missing: 921
- Partial: 819
- Source review: Bazel 9.3.2 (`5951e93c05876016377063a150f8b56f38276461`) versus zel (`2084b3f5a9bd343f38ffbc7633d65f21bab0f654`)
- Complete review: [bazel-code-differences.md](bazel-code-differences.md)

### `src/test/cpp/bazel_startup_options_test.cc`
- Bazel lines: 358
- Zel counterpart: `/workspace/zel-cursor/crates/zel-options/src/startup.rs`
- Verdict: partial
- Differences:
  - [P2] On macOS, `XDG_CACHE_HOME` is not used. With `TEST_TMPDIR` unset, the output user root is `$HOME/Library/Caches/bazel/_bazel_{user}` (or `/var/tmp/_bazel_{user}` when home is absent). The test expects `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/bazel/_bazel_{user}` on both Linux and Darwin.
  - [P2] `TEST_TMPDIR`, `XDG_CACHE_HOME`, and `HOME` are used as given. The no-shell-expansion cases expect those values prefixed with the cwd (`<cwd>/~/"$foo/test"/_bazel_gandalf`, `<cwd>/~/cache${bar}/bazel/_bazel_gandalf`, and the Linux `.cache` / macOS `Library/Caches` forms of `<cwd>/~/home$(echo baz)`), with `$`, quotes, and `$(...)` left unexpanded.
  - [P1] On Windows the test expects `output_user_root` `C:/Users/gandalf/_bazel_gandalf` from `HOME`, or from `USERPROFILE` when `HOME` is unset, and `install_base` `C:/Users/gandalf/install/deadbeef`. Resolution uses `%LOCALAPPDATA%/bazel/_bazel_{user}`, otherwise `{home}/AppData/Local/bazel/_bazel_{user}`, otherwise `C:/temp/_bazel_{user}`. The client reads `HOME` and does not read `USERPROFILE`. `install_base` is always `<output_user_root>/install/<md5>`.
  - [P2] `--block_for_lock=…` and `--noblock_for_lock=…` are accepted. The nullary check rejects them with `In argument '--block_for_lock=foo': option '--block_for_lock' does not take a value.`
  - [P2] With `--ignore_all_rc_files` left on, an explicit `--bazelrc` warns once (`WARNING: Value of --bazelrc is ignored, since --ignore_all_rc_files is on.`). An explicit `--workspace_rc` whose final value is on does not warn. The test also expects one following line, `WARNING: Explicit value of --workspace_rc is ignored, since --ignore_all_rc_files is on.`, including when both flags are repeated. The same warning function’s explicit `--home_rc` and `--system_rc` warnings are absent.
  - [P2] The client product name is `bazel`, and the output-root suffix is the fixed string `_bazel_`. The test requires the product name `Bazel`, lowercased only when building that suffix.
  - [P3] There is no JVM logging formatter. The test requires `com.google.devtools.build.lib.util.SingleLineFormatter`.

### `src/test/cpp/blaze_archive_test.cc`
- Bazel lines: 173
- Zel counterpart: `/workspace/zel-cursor/crates/zel-client/src/daemon_client.rs`
- Verdict: partial
- Differences:
  - [P2] Bazel `ExtractData` unpacks zip members `foo`, `bar`, and `path/to/subdir/baz` into the install base with those exact contents. Zel only creates the install-base directory and writes `install_base_key`; it never unpacks the binary zip.
  - [P2] After extraction, Bazel blesses those files so `IsUntampered` is true and each mtime is later than now plus nine years. Zel leaves normal filesystem mtimes and has no untampered check.
  - [P2] The first `ExtractData` returns a duration. A second call returns no duration when the install base already exists, every archived file is still untampered, and `install_base_key` matches the expected MD5. Zel always rewrites `install_base_key` and drops both `create_dir_all` and `write` errors, with no skip and no extraction-duration result.

### `src/test/cpp/blaze_util_posix_test.cc`
- Bazel lines: 212
- Zel counterpart: `/workspace/zel-cursor/crates/zel-server/src/sys.rs`
- Verdict: partial
- Differences:
  - [P1] `UnlimitResources` raises the soft limits of `RLIMIT_NOFILE` and `RLIMIT_NPROC` and is invoked unconditionally at client startup. Zel never adjusts those limits, so both `SuccessWithExplicitLimits` and `SuccessWithPossiblyInfiniteLimits` have no implementation.
  - [P2] With a finite hard limit (the explicit-limits case sets soft 1 and hard 8), Bazel sets only the soft limit to that hard limit. `unlimit_coredumps` writes `RLIM_INFINITY` into both soft and hard.
  - [P2] When the hard limit is `RLIM_INFINITY` and infinity is not allowed (`NOFILE`/`NPROC`), Bazel sets the soft limit to `GetExplicitSystemLimit` (`kern.maxfilesperproc` / `kern.maxprocperuid` on Darwin; `-1` on Linux/BSD, which skips that test). Zel has no kernel-cap lookup and would request infinity.
  - [P2] `UnlimitCoredumps` (`allow_infinity` true) raises only the soft `RLIMIT_CORE` to the existing hard limit, which may be finite, and the test requires the soft limit to leave 1. Zel always requests infinity for both fields, so a finite hard ceiling makes `setrlimit` fail and the soft limit stays 1.
  - [P2] Bazel returns false and logs a warning when `getrlimit` or `setrlimit` fails, and returns immediately when soft already equals hard. Zel ignores the `setrlimit` result and has no failure or already-equal path.
  - [P2] Bazel runs `UnlimitCoredumps` in the client when `--unlimit_coredumps` is set. Zel calls `unlimit_coredumps` only inside the background daemon for a truthy `--unlimit_coredumps=` value.

### `src/test/cpp/blaze_util_test.cc`
- Bazel lines: 294
- Zel counterpart: `/workspace/zel-cursor/crates/zel-options/src/startup.rs`
- Verdict: partial
- Differences:
  - [P2] `ReadFrom` reads a non-blocking pipe to EOF, retries `EAGAIN`/`EINTR`, and concatenates a second write that arrives after a delay as raw bytes. Zel has no such reader; `std::fs::read_to_string` fails on invalid UTF-8, and `WouldBlock` is not retried until the writer closes.
  - [P2] `SearchNullaryOption` returns the caller-supplied default when the flag is absent (both `false` and `true` are asserted), keeps scanning through non-options such as `build` and `:target`, and lets the last `--flag` / `--noflag` win until `--`. `--flag=value` aborts with `BAD_ARGV` (exit 2) and `In argument '--flag=value': option '--flag' does not take a value.`; the same form after `--` does not abort. Zel stops at the first non-option, uses a fixed per-flag default, and returns an error only for catalogued nullary startup options. `--block_for_lock=1` is accepted and parsed as a boolean; an unknown name is an unknown-startup-option error.
  - [P2] `GetAllUnaryOptionValues` keeps each value verbatim, in order, including a value that is itself `--flag`, and a final `--flag` with no following argument is recorded as the string `--flag`. Zel `ListString` conversion splits `--bazelrc` and `--host_jvm_args` on commas, and an empty `--flag=` becomes an empty list. A missing following argument is a startup-option-missing-value error.
  - [P1] With ignore-after `/dev/null`, the sentinel is kept and later values are dropped (`value1`, `/dev/null`, not `value3`). `/workspace/zel-cursor/crates/zel-options/src/rc.rs` skips a `/dev/null` entry and still loads later `--bazelrc` paths.

### `src/test/cpp/blaze_util_windows_test.cc`
- Bazel lines: 162
- Zel counterpart: `/workspace/zel-cursor/crates/zel-client/src/lib.rs`
- Verdict: partial
- Differences:
  - [P2] `GetPathEnv` turns `A\B c` into `A/B c` and strips a leading `\\?\`, `\\.\`, or `\??\` so `\\?\A:\B c` becomes `A:/B c`, leaving the drive letter’s case unchanged. Client env forwarding keeps those strings unchanged. `PathFragment::create` in `/workspace/zel-cursor/crates/zel-vfs/src/lib.rs` (used for `LOCALAPPDATA` in `/workspace/zel-cursor/crates/zel-options/src/startup.rs`) rewrites `\\?\A:\B c` to `/?/A:/B c` and uppercases drive letters (`c:\foo` → `C:/foo`).
  - [P2] `GetPathEnv` aborts with exit code 36 on a network path, a drive-relative path such as `c:foo`, or a leading `/`. Zel does not abort; `PathFragment` accepts those strings.
  - [P2] `SetEnv` / `UnsetEnv` use case-insensitive Windows names: setting `Bazel_TEST_Key1` is visible as `bazel_test_key1`, an empty value stays set, and `UnsetEnv` removes it, including names longer than `MAX_PATH`. Zel does not mutate the process environment this way. Forwarded `--client_env` entries are an exact, case-sensitive map, so those two names do not alias.
  - [P2] `GetEnv` / `SetEnv` convert UTF-16 with `CP_UTF8` and exit 37 if `CstringToWstring` or `WstringToCstring` fails. Zel drops a non-UTF-8 name or value (`into_string().ok()`), and `startup.rs` uses `to_string_lossy` (U+FFFD).

### `src/test/cpp/option_processor_test.cc`
- Bazel lines: 405
- Zel counterpart: `/workspace/zel-cursor/crates/zel-options/src/startup.rs`
- Verdict: partial
- Differences:
  - [P2] `SplitCommandLine` always stores `args[0]` as `path_to_binary` and starts startup options at index 1, so `mybazel` stays out of the command. `split_command_line` treats the first token as a startup flag or the command (`zel-client` omits the program name before the call). An empty vector is the error `Unable to split command line, args is empty` and `ParseOptions` returns `BAD_ARGV` (2). An empty slice returns success with an empty command and no command args.
  - [P2] `-h`, `-help`, and `--help` end startup parsing and are the command text, and later tokens stay command args (`help`, `-h`, `-help`, `--help`). Zel rewrites only `-h` and `--help` to the command `help` and drops every following token. `-help` is an unknown startup option and exits 2. A lone `--version` becomes the command `version` with `--startup_version`; in Bazel that token is an unknown startup option.
  - [P3] On Windows and Cygwin, parsed `host_jvm_args` starts with `-Dbazel.windows_unix_root=` plus each user value (`MyParam`, then `42` for the separate `--host_jvm_args` form). Zel’s vector starts empty and only appends the user values.
  - [P2] `--host_jvm_args` and `--bazelrc` keep one raw string per occurrence. Zel types both as `ListString` and comma-splits the value, so one flag with commas becomes multiple entries.
  - [P2] `DedupeBlazercPaths` canonicalizes, drops paths that do not canonicalize (`foo`, `""`), and keeps the first spelling when a relative path or symlink names the same file. `/workspace/zel-cursor/crates/zel-options/src/rc.rs` `discover_and_load_rc_files` dedupes with a `HashSet` of the path text as written, so those aliases are both loaded. A missing implicit rc is skipped. An unreadable explicit `--bazelrc` is exit 2.

### `src/test/cpp/rc_file_test.cc`
- Bazel lines: 1288
- Zel counterpart: `/workspace/zel-cursor/crates/zel-options/src/rc.rs`
- Verdict: partial
- Differences:

  - [P2] Legacy master rc files are not reported on a normal startup. The test expects `The following rc files are no longer being read` to include both `tools/bazel.rc` and `<binary dir>/bazel.bazelrc`. The client warning in `/workspace/zel-cursor/crates/zel-client/src/lib.rs` fires only for `%workspace%/.bazelrc` when `--noworkspace_rc` is set.
  - [P2] A repeated import is skipped and does not warn. The tests expect `WARNING: Duplicate rc file: ...` and a second read for the same canonical path, including `%workspace%/...`, `%workspace%///.//...`, `extra/../...`, a diamond import, and a file both imported and passed with `--bazelrc`.
  - [P1] `startup:linux`, `startup:macos`, `startup:windows`, `startup:freebsd`, and `startup:openbsd` are not applied to startup options. On a matching host the test expects that line to override `startup --max_idle_secs=1` and to appear in the provenance line. Only the plain `startup` section is applied.
  - [P2] `try-import-if-bazel-version` treats an unparseable build label such as `no_version` as a match, so the import runs. The test expects it to be skipped and `max_idle_secs` to stay 42.
  - [P1] Version checks drop prerelease identifiers and a leading `v`, and `~` means “same major and greater or equal” (`~1.2.3` accepts `1.3.0`). The tests expect `~1.2.3` to be `>=1.2.3 <1.3.0`, `~1.2` to be `<1.3.0`, prerelease ordering (`1.2.3-prerelease` is less than `1.2.3`; `==` / `!=` with a prerelease differ), and failure for `v1.2.3` / `v8.4.2` (`Could not parse the tilde range version` / `Could not parse version 'v8.4.2' as a valid semantic version`).
  - [P2] `try-import-if-bazel-version ==no_version ...` is reported as an invalid version condition (`Invalid target semantic version 'no_version'`). The test expects exit code 2 and `Invalid import declaration in config file` plus `Could not parse version 'no_version' as a valid semantic version`.
  - [P2] Grouped startup provenance on `--announce_rc` joins flags with `", "` (`--max_idle_secs=42, --io_nice_level=6`). The tests expect a single space, including across an import (`--max_idle_secs=42`, then the imported file, then `--io_nice_level=6`). The fatal path uses a space.
  - [P2] Rc file bytes are decoded with lossy UTF-8 before tokenization, so invalid UTF-8 becomes U+FFFD. The C++ client keeps the raw file bytes.

### `src/test/cpp/rc_options_test.cc`
- Bazel lines: 600
- Zel counterpart: `/workspace/zel-cursor/crates/zel-options/src/rc.rs`
- Verdict: partial
- Differences:
  - [P2] `ImportDiamond` expects the same file to be parsed twice (`startup` args `foo`, `bar`, `bar`, `foo`). Zel skips a path already in `visited`, so the second `startup_foo.bazelrc` import is dropped and the repeated `foo` is missing. `loaded_rc_files` is deduped the same way; Bazel appends each canonical path again.
  - [P1] `BadStartupLineContinuation_InterpretsNextLineAsNewline` keeps the next line as command `bar` with arg `baz` (plus the stray `" "` token). Zel only accepts a fixed command list and skips anything else, so `bar`/`baz` never appear.
  - [P1] `ImportedFileDoesNotExist` requires the error to name the import token literally (`'somefile'`) and, off Windows, the exact `(error: 2): No such file or directory` from the read of that path. Zel resolves a non-`%workspace%` import against the importing file’s directory and reports that resolved path, with the Unix ENOENT text hardcoded even when the host error differs.
  - [P2] File bytes are `String::from_utf8_lossy` and then scanned as Unicode scalars. Bazel keeps the raw byte string and tokenizes bytes, so invalid UTF-8 stays in the option text instead of becoming U+FFFD.

### `src/test/cpp/sem_ver_test.cc`
- Bazel lines: 97
- Zel counterpart: `/workspace/zel-cursor/crates/zel-options/src/rc.rs`
- Verdict: partial
- Differences:
  - [P1] `parse_semver` keeps only a `(u32, u32, u32)` core: it strips a leading `v`, drops everything after the first `-`, and fills a missing minor or patch with 0. Every pair in the test list that shares major.minor.patch therefore compares equal, including each prerelease against its release. The test requires prerelease precedence: numeric identifiers below non-numeric ones, numeric identifiers compared as integers (`beta.2` < `beta.11`), ASCII order otherwise, a longer identifier list above a proper prefix (`alpha` < `alpha.1`), and any prerelease below the release (`1.0.0-rc.1` < `1.0.0`, `1.2.3-zzz` < `1.2.3`). `==`, `!=`, `<`, `>`, `<=`, and `>=` disagree on that list.
  - [P1] `NextMinorVersion` is not applied. The test’s next-minor results (`0.0.0`→`0.1.0`, `8.0.0`→`8.1.0`, `8.2.4`→`8.3.0`, `8.2.4-beta`→`8.3.0`, prerelease cleared) are the upper bound Bazel uses for `~` when the target contains a dot (`~8.2` and `~8.2.4` are `< 8.3.0`). Rust `~` is only `major == target.major && current >= target`, so those ranges also accept `8.3.0` and later 8.x. `NextMajorVersion` (`8.2.4` and `8.2.4-beta`→`9.0.0`) is Bazel’s bound only for a dot-free target such as `~8`; Rust uses that same-major bound for every `~`. With the prerelease removed, `~8.2.4-beta` also matches `8.2.4-alpha`, which the test orders below `8.2.4-beta`.
  - [P2] Parse acceptance differs from the semver.org match the test relies on. Rust accepts partial versions (`8`, `8.1`) and a leading `v`, and rejects `1.2.3+build` because the patch token `3+build` fails `u32` parsing. C++ parses build metadata and ignores it in `Compare`, so `1.2.3+build` equals `1.2.3`. Components are `u32` rather than C++ `int`: a component above `INT_MAX` that still fits in `u32` parses in Rust and fails the C++ `int` capture. An unparseable current version makes `eval_bazel_version_condition` return true; Bazel skips the conditional import when `SemVer::Parse` fails.

### `src/test/cpp/startup_options_test.cc`
- Bazel lines: 229
- Zel counterpart: `/workspace/zel-cursor/crates/zel-options/src/startup.rs`
- Verdict: partial
- Differences:

  - [P3] Default `java_logging_formatter` is `com.google.devtools.build.lib.util.SingleLineFormatter`. Zel has no equivalent and does not configure JVM logging with that formatter.

Zel accepts `=true`/`=false` on boolean startup flags, and the server also turns command logging off for the exact raw string `--write_command_log=false`. `--nowrite_command_log` still disables the log in both.

### `src/test/cpp/util/file_posix_test.cc`
- Bazel lines: 328
- Zel counterpart: `/workspace/zel-cursor/crates/zel-client/src/daemon_client.rs`
- Verdict: partial
- Differences:
  - [P3] `PathExists` is absent. Bazel uses `access(F_OK)`: missing paths and `""` are false; `/`, `/usr`, `/usr/`, and `/usr/bin/yes` are true.
  - [P3] `CanReadFile`, `CanExecuteFile`, and `CanAccessDirectory` are absent. A directory is never a readable or executable file; directory access requires a directory with read, write, and execute (mode `0500` fails, `0700` succeeds). A file created by `fopen` is readable only; mode `0100` is executable and not readable, and is not a directory.
  - [P3] `ChangeDirectory` is absent. Bazel `chdir` returns false for a missing path, and `chdir("/usr")` leaves `getcwd` as `/usr`.
  - [P3] `ForEachDirectoryEntry` is absent. `opendir` failure, including a regular file, yields no entries. `.` and `..` are skipped. Symlink entries are not directories (`d_type != DT_DIR`, otherwise `lstat`). Listing a symlink to a directory follows it and reports children under that symlink path.
  - [P3] `RemoveRecursively` is absent. `lstat` treats a missing path (`ENOENT`) as success. A symlink, including a symlink to a directory, is unlinked and the target stays. A real directory is walked. A directory in mode `0500` that still contains a file fails and is left in place.
  - [P3] `CreateSiblingTempDir` is absent. Bazel uses `mkdtemp` on `<basename>.tmp.XXXXXX` in the same parent, leaves an existing parent at mode `0700` (mode `0777` only if the parent was missing), and sets the new directory to `0777 & ~umask`. Failure to create the parent dies with exit code 37; `mkdtemp` failure dies with exit code 36.
  - [P3] Live `MakeDirectories` checks match `make_directories`: nested create, child-only chmod to `mode & ~umask` (`0750`), `ENOTDIR` (20) for a file or a symlink to a file, success for a symlink to a directory, and `EACCES` (13) for `""` and `/`. `HammerMakeDirectories` has no live assertion.

Zel always uses `[FATAL timestamp src/main/cpp/blaze.cc:1275] …` and returns the caller’s code (2 for command-line fatals, 37 only for internal failures), with no arbitrary die code and no `FATAL:` form when debug logging is off.

### `src/test/cpp/util/strings_test.cc`
- Bazel lines: 332

- Verdict: partial

  - [P2] `Split` drops empty segments and keeps surrounding spaces (`" a, b "` is `" a"`, `" b "`). The `BAZELRC` split trims each comma-separated piece, so that value is `"a"`, `"b"`.

### `src/test/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/actions/ActionCacheCheckerTest.java`
- Bazel lines: 1972

- Verdict: partial
- Differences:
  - [P2] The test’s statistics are exact: `NOT_CACHED`, one `DIGEST_MISMATCH` for an action-key change, a used client-env change, a salt change, or an output-byte change, `CORRUPTED_CACHE_ENTRY` when `get` returns `Entry.CORRUPTED`, and `UNCONDITIONAL_EXECUTION` on every run of a volatile `executeUnconditionally` action (0 hits). Zel keeps no hit/miss counters. `must_execute` returns `DifferentActionKey`, `DifferentEnvironment`, `OutputsMissing`, `DifferentDeps`, or `DifferentFiles`, in that order, so a missing output is reported before an input-set or content change.
  - [P2] Any must-execute miss that already had an entry removes it before the action runs. An expired remote file, an expired tree child, an expired archived representation, a flipped `useArchivedTreeArtifacts` flag, or a metadata-disabled recheck of a missing output leaves `cache.get` null. Zel keeps the previous entry until a later successful `put_entry` or a failed execution.
  - [P1] `actionExecutionSalt` and the output permission mode are inside the cache digest. Zel’s action key and `must_execute` ignore both. Client env is only `getClientEnvironmentVariables()` (unused vars stay hits) for every action. Zel hashes `SpawnAction.inherited_env` names that exist in the client env, and file-write and other non-spawn actions ignore the client env.
  - [P1] With `storeOutputMetadata`, the entry stores remote file metadata and tree metadata (remote children only, remote archived file, resolved path) and a hit injects that metadata into the output store while the output path is absent. Local file and local archived metadata are omitted. An empty tree is a hit with no directory. A matching local tree child or archived file stays a hit and the injected value mixes local metadata for paths that exist with remote metadata for the rest. Zel stores local content-digest strings, treats a missing path as `OutputsMissing`, and does not inject remote, tree, archived, or resolved-path metadata. A remote-only output that is never created fails in Zel as “output was not created” (exit 1, entry removed) unless it is pending, and a pending missing output still cannot hit.
  - [P2] `OutputChecker.shouldTrustMetadata` false is a `DIGEST_MISMATCH`. `CHECK_TTL` rejects metadata whose expiration is missing or not after now, including one expired tree child or an expired archived representation, and drops the entry. Zel has no trust callback and no expiration.
  - [P2] Proxy outputs are recorded on the entry. A later check with null metadata in the store calls `ProxyMetadataFactory`: equal proxy metadata is a hit and is injected; a different proxy, a null return, or an `IOException` is a `DIGEST_MISMATCH` and the proxy path remains on the entry. Zel has no proxy-output set and no factory.
  - [P2] `CONSTANT_METADATA` outputs are compared as constant metadata when the file is readable, so only deletion (metadata `IOException` becomes null) forces a re-execution. Zel always hashes file bytes, so a content change misses as well.

A journal shortened by one byte is dropped: no event, no quarantine, and the map remains (size 301 = 300 entries plus the validation record). The map round-trips (the test’s 100-day steps from the epoch stay on minute boundaries, through 700 days). Zel entries have no timestamps, and `get` does not change access time.
  - [P2] Bazel `trim(threshold, maxAge)` drops entries strictly older than `now - maxAge` when `numStale != 0` and `numStale < threshold * actionMap.size()` is false. `actionMap.size()` includes the validation record, and the multiply is `float` (`0.2f * 5` is `1.0f`, so one stale entry of five is removed; `0.3f` keeps it). Threshold `0` removes every stale entry. The kept set is saved and reloaded. Zel has no trim.
  - [P2] Bazel `removeIf(Entry::discoversInputs)` removes entries whose discovered-input list is non-null, including an empty list, and the next full save persists that. Zel stores `discovered_inputs` as a `Vec<String>` and has no predicate removal, so an empty list cannot mean “does not discover inputs.”
  - [P2] Bazel `put`/`get` round-trips remote file metadata (digest, size, location index, expiration epoch millis or `-1` if absent, in-memory flag, optional resolved path), tree metadata with remote children only, a remote archived file only (local children and a local archived file are omitted), the tree resolved path, and proxy outputs as exec-path strings. Local file metadata is omitted, so `getOutputFile` is null. `discoversInputs` is part of the persisted entry (`toString` differs for true vs false). Zel stores an action-key string, a client-env digest, a metadata digest, a path-to-digest `BTreeMap`, and a discovered-path list. The simple `put` updates only `action_key`.

An implicit macro attribute default is checked like any other dep of the instantiation package: `//pkg`-only implicit deps are allowed and `//macros`-only implicit deps are rejected. Cases where the caller is the instantiation package still allow or deny as Bazel does.

- Verdict: partial

Zel hashes only after the full body is buffered and fails the download with `Checksum was <actual hex> but wanted <expected hex>` before writing the output.
  - [P3] A body of `PRECHECK_BYTES` (32768) + 70001 bytes with a bad checksum is returned from `create`; the `IOException` whose message contains `Checksum` is raised when a read hits EOF, before `close`. Zel applies the same full-body check and never yields a readable prefix of a mismatched payload.
  - [P2] With `Accept-Ranges` containing `bytes`, a `SocketTimeoutException` during that pre-read is resumed in place (a `Range: bytes=<offset>-` request only after some bytes were read, and then only if `Content-Range` starts with `bytes <offset>-`), at most 3 times; further timeouts propagate `SocketTimeoutException` after more than 3 attempts, and one timeout followed by a successful read returns the payload. Zel treats a read timeout as a retryable failure of the whole request (default 5 extra attempts) and surfaces `Error downloading [<url>] to <path>: ...`.
  - [P2] An interrupt flag set between `read` calls throws `InterruptedIOException` and stops the read. Zel does not observe the interrupt flag between reads.
  - [P2] `Content-Length` one byte above the body throws `ContentLengthMismatchException` with actual size equal to the bytes read and expected size equal to the header.   - [P2] `Content-Length` one byte below the readable body throws `ContentLengthMismatchException` with actual equal to the full body length and expected equal to length minus one, because every byte the stream yields is counted and compared at EOF. Zel reads at most `Content-Length` bytes and accepts that prefix.
  - [P2] `Content-Encoding: gzip` on a body that is not gzip throws `ZipException` from `create`. Zel’s HTTP reader fails with `Bad gzip content-encoding: Not in gzip format`. HTTPS goes through curl, so the failure text is curl’s content-decoding error.
  - [P2] `Content-Encoding: x-gzip` (exact set membership with `gzip`) on a URL with no compressed extension is decompressed to the original bytes. Zel’s HTTP reader decompresses only when the content-encoding equals `gzip`, ASCII case-insensitively, so `x-gzip` stays compressed.
  - [P1] Decompression is skipped when the connection URL or the original URL’s last extension is `gz` or `tgz`, or when the caller type is `tgz` or `tar.gz` (last extension `gz`/`tgz`). Type `tar` is still decompressed. Zel always gunzips `Content-Encoding: gzip` and has no type argument, so those `.tar.gz` / `.tgz` / `tar.gz` bodies are decompressed; curl on HTTPS does the same.

### `src/test/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/buildeventservice/AbstractBuildEventRecorder.java`

Every other event case or sequence, including an unset event, is `UNKNOWN` with no description. Zel’s in-memory server answers every lifecycle call with an empty message and gRPC status 0.
  - [P3] A lifecycle predicate can replace that status. If the predicate throws, the result is `INTERNAL` whose description is the exception message, including a null message. Zel has no lifecycle fault injection.

Zel acknowledges every decoded request immediately and sends status 0 only after the client ends the stream, including when the last event is not stream-finished.
  - [P3] Acknowledgements can be held and later flushed FIFO, then the current event’s acknowledgement is appended and the buffer is replaced. The default is to send immediately. Zel never batches an earlier acknowledgement onto a later response.
  - [P3] Each acknowledgement copies the request stream id and sequence. A switch instead acknowledges sequence + 1 and skips the normal status path. Zel always echoes the request sequence and omits `stream_id` when that field is absent.
  - [P3] Lifecycle events, all tool events, and successfully acknowledged tool events are kept in insertion order per stream id. Zel keeps two global arrival-order byte lists, with no per-stream split and no separate success list.
  - [P3] The inbound tool-stream failure is stored as a status that stays null until then; tests accept `CANCELLED` or `INTERNAL`. Zel does not retain that status.
  - [P3] The recorder binds a freshly chosen TCP port and reports -1 when no server is running. Zel uses an in-memory duplex and has no port.

A non-completing last event (and a close with no completing event) is `UNKNOWN_STATUS`; exit code 0 is `COMMAND_SUCCEEDED` and any other `BuildCompletingEvent` exit is `COMMAND_FAILED`. Zel has only those two results, defaults to succeeded, and does not derive status from the last event. Tool-stream sequence 1 carries the raw keyword set and `checkPrecedingLifecycleEvents=false`. Zel rewrites keywords to `command_name=`, `protocol_name=BEP`, and `user_keyword=`, puts them on every lifecycle RPC including invocation-finished, and forces `check_preceding_lifecycle_events_present` true.

Zel retries that unary call and then discards the error, still uploads the tool stream, and still publishes finish events after a successful stream.
  - [P2] Each lifecycle event failing once with `UNAVAILABLE` still completes, with ordered duplicates and finish status `UNKNOWN_STATUS`, and the tool stream is only `ComponentStreamFinished` sequence 1. Zel reports succeeded on that close, and the finish events are sequence 1.

Zel does not treat `CANCELLED` as retriable, so that stream fails on the first response. A successful ack resets the retry counter, so 13 events that each fail once with `UNAVAILABLE` still complete and the successful sequence numbers are exactly those 13. Zel’s stream attempt counter only increases, so the fifth stream failure aborts even when each failure made progress.
  - [P2] `INVALID_ARGUMENT` is not retried and is a persistent `BES_STREAM_NOT_RETRYING_FAILURE`. Stream `FAILED_PRECONDITION` is not retried and is a transient `BES_UPLOAD_TIMEOUT_ERROR`. Zel returns the gRPC status string for the first two, and on OK with missing acks it resends until the retry cap and then returns `BES upload failed: not all events were acknowledged`.
  - [P2] An acknowledgement whose sequence is not the next expected one fails the upload immediately with transient `BES_UPLOAD_TIMEOUT_ERROR` and status `FAILED_PRECONDITION`, with no retry. Zel’s `close` finishes with `Build Event Service upload timed out (--bes_timeout)`, and that same timeout also bounds the connector and lifecycle RPCs.

The tests require one upload per distinct path (duplicate paths collapse to one map entry), `named_set_of_files` URIs `cas://` plus the digest of the Latin-1 file bytes, and a failed second upload that is not retried: `close` fails transiently with `BES_UPLOAD_LOCAL_FILE_ERROR` whose cause is the `IOException` (`File upload failed.`), and the server stream error is `CANCELLED` or `INTERNAL`. Zel serializes the BEP event and does not upload referenced files.

### `src/test/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/buildeventservice/BuildEventServiceTransportGrpcTest.java`
- Bazel lines: 192
- Zel counterpart: `/workspace/zel-cursor/crates/zel-events/src/bes.rs`
- Verdict: partial
- Differences:
  - [P3] Bazel serves a real plaintext gRPC endpoint on a free TCP port (`localhost:<port>`, no call credentials, no interceptor) and refuses to build the client unless that port is greater than 0 (`getPort()` is `-1` when the server is down). Zel’s fake BES is an in-memory HTTP/2 pair with authority `bes.local` and never binds a port.
  - [P2] With out-of-order acknowledgements enabled, Bazel ACKs `sequence_number + 1` and does not record the event as successful. The upload then fails once, with gRPC `FAILED_PRECONDITION`, exit `TRANSIENT_BUILD_EVENT_SERVICE_UPLOAD_ERROR`, and `BES_UPLOAD_TIMEOUT_ERROR`. Zel treats any ACK whose sequence is greater than `acked` as progress, so `sequence + 1` advances the cursor and can mark the stream fully acknowledged.
  - [P2] A null stream status still records the event and sends any buffered ACKs, but Bazel half-closes the RPC only when the status is non-null and OK. A predicate that always returns null therefore leaves the stream open and `close()` throws `TimeoutException`. Zel always finishes the tool stream with `grpc-status: 0`.
  - [P2] Bazel’s lifecycle default is OK only for sequence 1 on `BuildEnqueued` and `InvocationAttemptStarted`, and sequence 2 on `InvocationAttemptFinished` and `BuildFinished`; every other lifecycle event is `UNKNOWN`. The tool stream is completed only for `COMPONENT_STREAM_FINISHED`. Zel accepts every lifecycle call with status 0 and ends the tool stream after the messages in that call.
  - [P2] Injected `INVALID_ARGUMENT` on the tool stream is not retried and exits `PERSISTENT_BUILD_EVENT_SERVICE_UPLOAD_ERROR` / `BES_STREAM_NOT_RETRYING_FAILURE`. Stream `FAILED_PRECONDITION` exits transient / `BES_UPLOAD_TIMEOUT_ERROR`. Lifecycle `FAILED_PRECONDITION` exits persistent / `BES_STREAM_NOT_RETRYING_FAILURE`. An OK trailers frame with ACKs still outstanding is not retried, exits persistent / `BES_STREAM_COMPLETED_WITH_UNACK_EVENTS_ERROR`, and the client status is `FAILED_PRECONDITION`. Zel retries only `UNKNOWN`, `DEADLINE_EXCEEDED`, `ABORTED`, `INTERNAL`, `UNAVAILABLE`, and `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` (stream budget 4, then `"BES upload failed: not all events were acknowledged"`). An OK stream with missing ACKs is resent. Any BES close error becomes exit `TRANSIENT_BUILD_EVENT_SERVICE_UPLOAD_ERROR`; persistent exit 45 and those `BuildProgress` codes are not produced. A close deadline uses `"Build Event Service upload timed out (--bes_timeout)"`.
  - [P3] Bazel records every attempt in a per-`StreamId` insertion-order multimap, including failures, and a separate successful-event multimap. `UNAVAILABLE` lifecycle retries are stored twice per event, in order. Zel’s UNAVAILABLE case returns before appending, so the failed attempt is absent, and the test only checks that the later successful stream has at least five requests and exactly four lifecycle messages.
  - [P2] Bazel sets `publishBuildToolEventStreamAccepted` when the RPC is accepted, before any message. A client `onError` is stored via `Status.fromThrowable`. A failed local-file upload is expected to surface there as `CANCELLED` or `INTERNAL`, with exit transient / `BES_UPLOAD_LOCAL_FILE_ERROR` and cause `"File upload failed."`. Zel drops unexpected stream events and has no client-cancel status.
  - [P1] This harness fixes the VFS digest to SHA256. File-upload cases write bytes with Latin-1, publish `cas://` plus the SHA-256 of the UTF-8 strings `"file1"` and `"file2"`, and collapse duplicate paths to one upload. Zel’s BES tests do not upload local files or check digests.
  - [P3] Bazel can withhold ACKs until a later request (batch mode) and, if lifecycle handling throws, return `INTERNAL` with that exception’s message. Zel ACKs each tool-stream message immediately and has no lifecycle `INTERNAL` path.

  - [P2] Multi-package-path planting is absent. Packages from more than one root do not split shared directories, and children are not linked from the longest package prefix. The planted set in that test (`pkgA`, `dir1/pkgA`, `dir1/pkgB`, `dir2/pkg/file`, `dir2/pkg/pkg`, `pkgB/file`, `pkgB/dir/file`, `pkgB/dir/pkg`, `pkgB/pkg`) is not produced.
  - [P2] Partial main-repo planting is absent. Without the root package, Bazel links only top-level directories that are prefixes of packages in the map (`dir1`, `dir2`, `dir3`) and leaves on-disk `dir4` and a root `file` unlinked. Zel links every top-level workspace entry.
  - [P2] Sibling repository layout is absent (`experimental_sibling_repository_layout` is a no-op). External repos stay at `execroot/external/<repo>` and are not siblings `execroot/../<repo>`; symlinks in the execroot’s parent are not removed first. An existing `execroot/external/<repo>` link is left as-is rather than replaced. Repos with and without a top-level package still become one symlink to the repo root, but the combined planted-path list the tests assert (main-repo links plus `external/X`, `external/Y`, `external/Z`) is not returned: the forest returns unplanted lowercase conflict names, and the external helper returns only external link paths.

  - [P2] `deleteTreesBelowNotPrefixed` still keeps names that start with the prefix and deletes the rest without following symlinks, so the `file-` / `a-dir` case matches for UTF-8 names. The prefix check uses lossy UTF-8 (`to_string_lossy`) rather than the filesystem basename as a Java string (Unix Latin-1 bytes): a non-UTF-8 name whose bytes start with the prefix is deleted. An unreadable directory is not made readable and retried; removal fails with the OS error.

### `src/test/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/concurrent/CancellableTaskTest.java`

  - [P3] Zel has no `CancellableTask`. `runIfNotCancelled` may run the body only once and returns true; a second call throws `IllegalStateException`. Cancel before start (`cancelAndAwait`, or `requestCancellation` then `awaitCompletion`) makes `runIfNotCancelled` return false and skips the body. A second cancel before or after a finished run returns without blocking.
  - [P3] Cancel during the body interrupts it and does not return until the body finishes. `requestCancellation` alone interrupts and returns while the body is still running. A later `awaitCompletion` waits without a second interrupt, so post-interrupt cleanup is not aborted. If `cancelAndAwait` is interrupted while waiting, it throws `InterruptedException`; a retry interrupts the still-running body again and waits until it finishes.
  - [P3] The optional completion action runs once, after the body, including when the body throws `IOException` with message `"task failed"` (that exception still propagates). Cancel before start also runs completion once; a repeated cancel or a prevented run does not run it again. A second canceller, and a `runIfNotCancelled` that loses the claim, both wait until that completion finishes; the losing run returns false. Cancellation during completion waits for it and does not interrupt it.
  - [P3] Cancel from the body or from completion throws `IllegalStateException`. `runIfNotCancelled` from the cancel-before-start completion throws `IllegalStateException`. Completion throwing `IllegalStateException` with message `"completion failed"` propagates from `runIfNotCancelled` or from the cancel call, then still marks the task terminal: a later cancel returns, and `runIfNotCancelled` returns false.
  - [P3] `runIfNotCancelled` on an already cancelled task returns false and restores the caller’s interrupt status (`Thread.interrupted()` stays true). With one runner and two `cancelAndAwait` callers, exactly one claim wins: the body runs at most once, completion runs exactly once, and `runIfNotCancelled` is true only when the body ran. A normal return from cancel means the body is not running and completion has finished.

### `src/test/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/exec/ParameterFileTest.java`

Zel has no such helper. A param file path is `{primary output exec path}-{chunk index}.params` (for example `bazel-out/k8-fastbuild/bin/a/out-0.params`), where the suffix is the 0-based index of that argument group, not the constant `"2"`.

Arguments are encoded with the given charset, reinterpreted as ISO-8859-1, written as those raw bytes plus `\n`, then decoded with the same charset. `--foo` and `--bar` round-trip for both ISO-8859-1 and UTF-8. `--füü` round-trips for both (ISO-8859-1 stores `ü` as the single byte `0xFC`; UTF-8 stores `C3 BC`). `--lambda=λ` becomes `--lambda=?` under ISO-8859-1 (`?` replaces unmappable U+03BB) and stays `--lambda=λ` under UTF-8. Zel `render_param_file` always emits UTF-8 (`into_bytes()`), has no ISO-8859-1 mode, never rewrites `λ` to `?`, and always writes `ü` as UTF-8 `C3 BC`.
  - [P1] `flagsOnly` of `["a", "--b", "--c=d", "e"]` is `["--b", "--c=d"]` in that order; `nonFlags` is `["a", "e"]` in that order. A flag is only an argument that starts with `"--"` (`--c=d` is a flag). Zel has no `flagsOnly` / `nonFlags` split. Param-file bodies contain every argument after `leading_args` (a prefix count), including positionals. `ParamFileFormat::FlagPerLine` is rendered the same as `Multiline`: the raw argument plus `\n`, with no `--` filter.

### `src/test/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/exec/StableSortTest.java`

An `actual_outputs` path that matches any `inputs` path forces the producer first (one of several outputs is enough; extra inputs do not drop the edge), including when that reverses lexicographic order (`b` then `a` becomes producer `b` before consumer `a`, and input order does not matter). With none it is the stripped proto of `command_args`, `environment_variables`, `platform`, `inputs`, and `mnemonic`, so no-output inputs `a` then `b` stay that order when the stream is `b`, `a`, and command args `b`, `e`, `f` follow the listed group. A dependency overrides that group: `d`, `a`, `c`, then `b`, `e`, `f`.
  - [P2] Locked graph orders that are not reproduced: `c`, `b`, `a`; `a`, `c`, `b`; `c`, `a`, `b` (including one spawn listing both `c1` and `c2`); `c`, `b`, `a`, `f`, `e`, `d`; `b`, `c`, `a`, `d`, `f`, `e`; `d`, `f`, `e`, `b`, `c`, `a`. Two producers of the same output `c` both precede the consumer, and equal key `1_c` keeps input order `a` then `b`.

Zel reads the finished log once in `emit_test_live` after the test action returns and appends it to stdout.
  - [P2] A log with no header and no trailing newline, `"blahblahblah"`, is copied verbatim to stdout and stderr stays empty. The same extra newline is added for any non-empty post-filter payload that does not end in `\n`. `"random\nlines\n"`, `"included\nlines\n"`, and an empty file match, and stderr stays empty.

Bazel treats it as a header only when that line ends in `\n` (`\r` stays in the line, so a CRLF delimiter does not match). A delimiter with no trailing `\n` leaves `foundHeader()` false, and `close()` then copies the whole file to stdout. Zel strips one trailing `\r` and treats a final delimiter line with no `\n` as a header, so the suffix is empty and nothing is written.

When no header was seen, the whole file is still copied to stdout after that wait. Zel has no interrupt flag, no 30-second wait, and no that error. If a header was already seen, Bazel does not reread the file, so bytes not yet pumped are dropped. Zel emits the full stripped log.
  - [P2] An `IOException` while pumping writes `"Failure reading or writing: "` plus the exception message and `\n` to stdout. A failed `std::fs::read` in Zel writes nothing.

  - [P3] `create` writes missing files as ISO-8859-1, one `\n` after every argument (zero arguments write a 0-byte file) and creates parents. If the path exists and there are zero lines, it leaves the bytes unchanged. If it exists and lines are non-empty, it compares `String.trim()` (code units `<= 0x20`) of the new `\n`-joined text with the raw Latin-1 file; a match keeps the bytes, a mismatch throws `IOException` `Conflict: '<relativePath>':\n'<newContent>'\n vs \n'<existingContent>'` with untrimmed texts. Reading a directory fails as an I/O error, not that conflict text.
  - [P3] `overwrite` `deleteTree`s an existing path, then `create`. `append` throws `IllegalArgumentException` `DO NOT write into the WORKSPACE file in mocks. If that is missing it tries `../READONLY/_main/` under the mock root; if that is also missing it throws `IOException` `target does not exist ` plus the original runfiles path. It creates parents, `delete`s only the destination node (not `deleteTree`), and symlinks to that absolute target (`SymlinkTargetType.UNSPECIFIED`).

A path that is empty or contains `./`, `../`, or `//` throws `IllegalArgumentException` (`path is not normalized: "%s"`). Manifest lookup of a missing runfile returns null and then NPEs; directory mode returns `RUNFILES_DIR/_main/...` even when absent, and the later read throws `IOException`. Lines are split on `\n`, `\r`, and `\r\n` (Guava `LineBuffer`; a trailing break does not add an extra empty line) and rewritten with `\n` only, so a source with no trailing break gains one. `overwrite` replaces the destination.
  - [P3] `copyDirectory` walks the native source with `Files.walk(source, depth)` (depth `0` is only the start; a negative depth throws `IllegalArgumentException`), does not follow directory symlinks, and keeps only `isFile()` entries whose relative path is non-empty, in walk order. A relative path that `endsWith("BUILD")` when `useEmptyBuildFiles` is true is `create`d with no lines (missing becomes 0 bytes; an existing file is left as-is). Other files are `copyTool`’d to `to + "/" + relative`. An `IOException` from a copy is rethrown as `RuntimeException` with that exception as the cause. `copyTools` and `linkTools` run in argument order and stop at the first failure.

### `src/test/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/profiler/MemoryProfilerTest.java`

  - [P2] Outside `ProfilePhase.FINISH`, and on `FINISH` when the parameters are null: one `gc()`, then one heap sample and one non-heap sample, and no sleeps. `"1,10"` on `FINISH` is the same, because the only iteration of the first pair is skipped.   - [P2] `"3,10"` on `FINISH` sleeps `10` seconds, then `10` seconds, in that order. Across the preceding `ANALYZE` call plus `FINISH`, `gc()` and heap reads run 4 times. The second subtraction therefore still contains the trimmed `//p:alias`.

Bazel’s exception message is the raw string, and the command line is `Error doing post analysis query: <message>` (no `Evaluation failed:`) with exit code 1 (`PARSING_FAILURE`).

A compressed mismatch is `compressed write incomplete: committed_size %d is neither -1 nor total %d - %s`. A server that completes before the client finishes (including `committed_size` 10 for a longer blob, or a stream that only holds the first chunk) succeeds and the committed size is not checked.

### `src/test/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/remote/ReaderPreferringReadWriteLockTest.java`
- Bazel lines: 357
- Zel counterpart: `none`
- Verdict: missing
- Differences:
  - [P3] Ten shared readers may all hold the lock at once. After every reader unlocks, a writer can lock and unlock.
  - [P3] Unlocking a read or write lock that the caller does not hold throws `IllegalMonitorStateException`. Unlocking the other mode while one mode is held also throws `IllegalMonitorStateException`.
  - [P3] A reader blocks while a writer holds the lock, and a writer blocks while a reader holds it. The waiter acquires exactly once after release, and the original mode can lock again.
  - [P3] A second writer blocks until the first writer unlocks, then acquires exactly once.
  - [P3] While a writer waits on an existing reader, another reader is still admitted. The writer acquires only after every reader unlocks, then both modes can lock again.
  - [P3] If a new reader locks after the last reader drops the count but before the writer is woken, the writer waits again and is not stranded. It acquires only after that new reader unlocks.
  - [P3] A blocked reader or writer interrupted while waiting throws `InterruptedException` and does not take the lock. The holder still owns it, and after unlock both modes can lock.
  - [P3] Interrupting the only writer waiting on a reader leaves later readers off the intrinsic monitor: three read lock/unlock cycles must not enter `BLOCKED` while another thread holds `synchronized` on the lock.
  - [P3] A thread already interrupted before `lockReadInterruptibly` or `lockWriteInterruptibly` throws `InterruptedException` and does not take the lock. The other mode can then lock and unlock. The interrupt status is cleared afterward.
  - [P3] Sixteen threads, each seeded `Random(0)` through `Random(15)` and running 20,000 iterations, take a write with probability 1/4 and a read otherwise. A writer must observe exactly one writer and zero readers. A reader must observe zero writers. Any `InterruptedException` is a violation. After all threads finish, violations, readers, and writers are all 0.

Zel stops when `attempt >= max_retries` instead of returning a negative delay.

Zel `run` only returns `Result<T, GrpcStatus>` and `std::thread::sleep` does not observe an interrupt or pass through a separate interruption error.

A `NOT_FOUND` status while an operation name is set clears the name and retries without checking `max_retries`, so `--remote_retries=0` still retries that case.

### `src/test/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/remote/RetrierTest.java`
- Bazel lines: 454
- Zel counterpart: `/workspace/zel-cursor/crates/zel-remote/src/grpc.rs`
- Verdict: partial
- Differences:
  - [P2] No circuit breaker. With `ZeroBackoff(3)` and a breaker that trips after 2 consecutive failures, Bazel stops and throws `CircuitBreakerException` (not `"call failed"`), leaves `consecutiveFailures == 2` and state `REJECT_CALLS`, and does not consume the remaining retries. `TRIAL_CALL` runs once: success returns `10` and moves to `ACCEPT_CALLS`; failure is not retried and `consecutiveFailures` becomes `1`. `REJECT_CALLS` rejects before the callable runs.
  - [P2] An interrupted thread throws `InterruptedException` (null message) and does not invoke the callable (`numCalls == 0`). A thrown `InterruptedException` is not retried (`numCalls == 1`) and is not classified, so neither `recordFailure` nor `recordSuccess` runs. `RetryPolicy::run` does not check interruption.
  - [P2] `EXPERIMENTAL_GRPC_RESULT_CLASSIFIER`: `ABORTED`, `UNKNOWN`, and `DEADLINE_EXCEEDED` are each tried 3 times (`ZeroBackoff(2)`) and every attempt increments consecutive failures (total 9, then `REJECT_CALLS`). `PERMISSION_DENIED`, `UNIMPLEMENTED`, `DATA_LOSS`, and `OUT_OF_RANGE` are tried once each and each increments consecutive failures until `REJECT_CALLS`. `NOT_FOUND` and `ALREADY_EXISTS` are not retried but count as success: `consecutiveFailures` resets to `0` and state becomes `ACCEPT_CALLS`, while the status exception still fails the call (`ExecutionException` on the async path). Zel retries the first three and does not retry the others, with no success-versus-permanent split and no breaker. `RemoteClient::execute` also retries `NOT_FOUND` after an operation name is known by clearing that name and calling `Execute` again.
  - [P2] A classifier that marks every error success performs one call, rethrows message `"call failed"`, calls `recordSuccess` once, and never `recordFailure`. Exhausted retries (`maxRetries=2`) perform 3 calls, rethrow `"call failed"`, call `recordFailure` 3 times, and never `recordSuccess`. Success on the third call returns `1`, with 2 `recordFailure` calls and 1 `recordSuccess`. Zel returns the last `GrpcStatus` (unit-test message `"x"`) after `max_retries + 1` attempts and has no breaker callbacks.
  - [P2] Async failures fail the future with `ExecutionException` whose cause message is `"call failed"` or `""` (`new Exception("")`). Zel returns `Err(GrpcStatus)` from synchronous `run` and does not wrap a cause whose message is empty.

### `src/test/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/remote/grpc/DynamicConnectionPoolTest.java`
- Bazel lines: 266
- Zel counterpart: `/workspace/zel-cursor/crates/zel-remote/src/grpc.rs`
- Verdict: partial

  - [P2] With `maxConcurrencyPerConnection` 1, two subscribed `create()` calls both complete: the first underlying connection is `connection0`, the second is `connection1`, and `connectionFactory.create` runs twice. `Channel::pick_conn` reuses the least-loaded connection while `active_streams() < STREAMS_PER_CONN` (`100`). Two checkouts that have not opened 100 local streams share that connection, and `connector.connect` runs once. Another connection is opened only when every pooled connection already has at least 100 active streams and `conns.len() < max_connections` (`max_connections.max(1)`).
  - [P2] While the first factory `Single` is still pending (`Thread.sleep(Integer.MAX_VALUE)`, subscriber `assertEmpty`, `terminated` stays false), the next `create()` completes on `connection1` and the factory count is 2. `pick_conn` holds the pool mutex across `connector.connect()` and the HTTP/2 handshake, so the second caller waits until that dial returns. A `connect` that never returns leaves the second caller waiting on the same mutex.
  - [P2] `SharedConnection.close()` returns the checkout, and the next `create()` completes on the same `connection0` with the factory count still 1. Zel frees capacity when the HTTP/2 stream’s `active_local` count drops. `Conn::close` sends GOAWAY and `fail("connection closed locally")`; `pick_conn` then drops connections for which `is_closed()` is true and dials again.
  - [P2] `close()` then `create()` fails the subscriber with `IllegalStateException` whose message contains `"closed"` (the pool throws `IllegalStateException("closed")`). `Channel::close` drains the current connections and closes them, and the next `pick_conn` dials a new one. Dial failures are gRPC status `UNAVAILABLE` with `"connection failed: {e}"` or `"h2 handshake failed: {e}"`.
  - [P2] `close()` during a pending create disposes the factory subscription (`canceled` becomes true), interrupts the sleeper so `finished` stays false, and fails the subscriber with `IllegalStateException` whose message contains `"closed"`. `Channel::close` takes the same mutex, so it runs after `connect` returns; that `pick_conn` already returned `Ok(conn)`. `Conn::close` then fails the connection with `io::Error` kind `ConnectionAborted` and message `"connection closed locally"`. `io_to_status` maps that to `UNAVAILABLE` and `"transport error: connection closed locally"`.

Bazel `ShellUtils.shellEscape`s each option and joins them with one space into a single `NestedSet` element of order `NAIVE_LINK_ORDER` (empty input is an empty set of that order). For this test the only element is `-source 8 -target 8 -Xmx1G '--arg=val' '-XepExcludedPaths:.*/\\$$?\\$$?AutoValue(Gson)?_.*\.java'`, and `tokenizeJavaOptions` on that set returns the original seven tokens in that order. Zel only has `java_tokenize_opts`, which reverses the depset and then tokenizes, so separate flags come out reversed instead of being joined and restored in source order. Zel's `shell_escape` is `ShellEscaper`, not `ShellUtils.shellEscape`: a non-leading `~` stays unquoted, and non-ASCII letters and digits are quoted.

Inside double quotes Zel always drops a backslash and keeps the next character; Bazel keeps the backslash unless the next character is `\` or `"`. On failure both keep the raw string. The thrown texts differ (`"unterminated escape"` and `"unterminated quotation in: {s}"` versus `"backslash at end of string"` and `"unterminated quotation"`) and are swallowed by `tokenizeJavaOptions`.

A path starting with `third_party/java` is rooted again on the suffix when that suffix has a source root. Bazel keeps the `java` segment of `third_party/java` when it is the first known root and is neither index 0 nor `src`, so `third_party/java/src/com/foo/Bar.java` is `src/com/foo/Bar.java` in Bazel and `com/foo/Bar.java` in Zel.

Nested sets are posted before parents, each set once, under concurrency. Splitting uses `--build_event_max_named_set_of_file_entries` (default 5000); values below 2 do not split. Zel does not expand sets inside the streamer. `BepBuilder::named_sets` splits a flat list when `max > 0` (so 1 splits) and URIs are percent-encoded `file://` (`file:///a%20b/c`).

Bazel also posts a successful `ExtraAction` when the flag is false. Zel's `publish_all_actions` flag is not read by `post`; the action observer publishes on `!success || publish_all`, so a successful extra action is omitted.
  - [P3] `consumeAsPairs` on empty/empty invokes the last consumer once with `(null, null)`. Zel `pairs` returns no pairs. Completion still emits one empty final progress, so a quiet close matches; the helper result does not. Non-empty pairing matches, and the last pair at completion is a childless final progress while earlier pairs announce the next progress id.

It hardcodes `/bin/bash`, ignores `--shell_executable`, and never emits `shExecutable must be non-null`.
  - [P1] Linux `--script_path` text is `#!/<shExecutable>`, then `cd <ShellEscaper(workingDir)> && \`, `exec env \`, sorted `-u UNSET_ME` / `-u UNSET_ME_TOO`, then sorted `ENV_VAR=val` / `ENV_VAR_WITH_SPACES='foo bar'`, then the escaped command and `"$@"` with no trailing newline. With the prefix `unescaped run-under prefix &&`, the command becomes `/bin/bash -c 'unescaped run-under prefix && executable argv1 '\''arg w spaces'\''' "$@"`. Zel’s script is always `#!/bin/bash`, quotes `cd` the same way for safe characters, and emits sorted `-u` / `KEY=value` lines, but the clear list also includes `JAVA_RUNFILES`, `RUNFILES_DIR`, `RUNFILES_MANIFEST_FILE`, `RUNFILES_MANIFEST_ONLY`, and `TEST_SRCDIR`, keys are not shell-escaped, the command is the absolute executable (or `external/bazel_tools/tools/test/test-setup.sh ./<name>` for a test) with no baked-in `argv1` / `'arg w spaces'`, and a run-under prefix is omitted from the script.
  - [P2] Windows `formatArgv` without a prefix leaves argument 0 raw and `windowsEscapeArg`s the rest, so `C:/unescaped executable`, `argv1`, `"arg w spaces"` is legal with a null shell. With a prefix it throws `IllegalArgumentException` `shExecutable must be non-null when --run_under is used` if the shell is null; otherwise it returns `[shExecutable, "-c", windowsEscapeArg(...)]`, tested as `unescaped /bin/bash`, `-c`, `"unescaped run-under prefix && 'C:/unescaped executable' argv1 'arg w spaces'"`. Zel has no Windows argv form.
  - [P1] Windows `--script_path` text starts `@echo off`, `cd /d workingDir` with `workingDir` unescaped, then `SET UNSET_ME=`, `SET UNSET_ME_TOO=`, `SET ENV_VAR=val`, `SET ENV_VAR_WITH_SPACES=foo bar` (values not quoted), then either `C:\executable argv1 "arg w spaces" %*` or, for prefix `echo hello &&`, `/bin/bash -c 'echo hello && C:\executable argv1 "arg w spaces"' %*`, with `/` changed to `\` only on the executable and no trailing newline. Zel never emits `@echo off`, `cd /d`, `SET`, or `%*`.

### `src/test/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/server/CommandManagerTest.java`
- Bazel lines: 189
- Zel counterpart: `/workspace/zel-cursor/crates/zel-server/src/daemon.rs`
- Verdict: partial
- Differences:
  - [P2] Bazel command ids are `UUID.randomUUID()` strings (`UUID.fromString` accepts them), and two nested `createCommand()` calls get different ids. Zel ids are `{server_pid}-{n}` with `next_id` starting at `1`, so the first Run is `{pid}-1`, then `{pid}-2`.
  - [P2] `isEmpty()` is true only when every `RunningCommand` is closed. Two commands may be open together, and after the inner close `isEmpty()` stays false until the outer close. Zel’s `running` count likewise stays non-zero for every in-flight Run, including one blocked on the lock, but the second command does not run beside the holder: it waits, or with `block_for_lock` false it fails with stderr `"Another command ({other}) is running. Exiting immediately.\n"` (`{other}` is `client_description`, or `"unknown"`). The wait text is `"Another command ({other}) is running. Waiting for it to complete on the server (server_pid={pid})...\n"`.
  - [P2] `waitForChange()` wakes on every register and every close, so two nested commands produce notification counts 1, 2, 3, then 4, including the create and the inner close that leave the map non-empty. Interrupting that waiter throws `InterruptedException` and ends the loop. Zel signals its condition variable when the exclusive lock is dropped and on Cancel. The idle loop polls `accept` every 20ms, and a lock waiter uses `wait_timeout` of 500ms plus a cancel flag.
  - [P2] With `doIdleServerTasks=true`, a command that registers an `IdleTask` named `"my idle task"` (default `delay()` `Duration.ZERO`) runs it as soon as that command’s close empties the map, before the next command. Starting the next command snapshots results in registration order and leaves them stored if that command never calls `getIdleTaskResults()`. The command after that sees exactly one result, name `"my idle task"`, status `SUCCESS`, and that call clears the list, so the following command gets null. A command that registers no tasks does not start an idle period and does not drop unretrieved results. With `doIdleServerTasks=false`, `setIdleTasks` does not run the task and the next `getIdleTaskResults()` is null. Zel `--idle_server_tasks` defaults to `true` (help `"Run System.gc() when the server is idle"`). When it is on, Zel waits until `running == 0` and `last_activity` has elapsed at least 10s, then once calls `save_to_disk` on the action cache. It keeps no name, status, or duration and does not hand a result to the next command. `idle_tasks_done` is set back to false when `last_activity` has elapsed under 1s. `--idle_server_tasks=false` skips that save.

An idle `poll` is an empty `Vec`.

### `src/test/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/skyframe/OutputsInvalidationIntegrationTest.java`
- Bazel lines: 228
- Zel counterpart: `none`
- Verdict: missing
- Differences:
  - [P3] Bazel installs an `OutputService` whose `startBuild` `ModifiedFileSet` is the only output-invalidation signal (`ActionFileSystemType.DISABLED`). `NOTHING_MODIFIED` skips every output check: the second build of `genrule(name='foo', outs=['foo.out'], cmd='touch $@')` does not emit `Executing genrule //foo:foo`, whether or not `foo.out` was deleted. Zel has no `startBuild` report. `CompactPersistentActionCache::must_execute` always digests every declared output, so a missing output is `OutputsMissing` (`output file(s) missing`) and the genrule re-executes.
  - [P2] `--experimental_check_output_files` defaults to true. When it is false, any report other than `EVERYTHING_DELETED` is replaced with `NOTHING_MODIFIED` before the check. `EVERYTHING_DELETED` still forces invalidation with the flag false (empty or deleted output tree). The exercised matrix, after deleting `foo.out`, re-executes and emits `Executing genrule //foo:foo` for (`everythingDeleted=false`, `--experimental_check_output_files=true`, `EVERYTHING_MODIFIED`), then (`true`, `false`, `EVERYTHING_DELETED`), then (`true`, `true`, `EVERYTHING_DELETED`). The omitted pair (`EVERYTHING_MODIFIED` with the flag false) does not re-execute. Zel lists the flag with default `true` and never reads it, so `--experimental_check_output_files=false` does not suppress checks and there is no `EVERYTHING_DELETED` exception.
  - [P3] Identical outputs are not invalidated when `startBuild` reports `EVERYTHING_MODIFIED`, `EVERYTHING_DELETED`, or a single `modify(artifact.getExecPath())`, including with `--experimental_check_output_files` set. The second build does not contain `Executing genrule //foo:foo`. Zel reaches the same skip only because the stored digest matches (`UpToDate`); a content change that the output service did not report is `DifferentFiles` (`one of the files has changed`) and re-executes. Zel's `ModifiedFileSet` is `Nothing` or source `FILE_STATE` / `DIRECTORY_LISTING_STATE` keys, not output-tree `EVERYTHING_MODIFIED`, `EVERYTHING_DELETED`, or per-exec-path modify, and `ActionExecutionFunction` recomputes only when inputs change.
  - [P3] With `//foo:foo` and `//foo:bar` (`touch $@`), deleting only `foo.out` and reporting only that exec path re-executes `//foo:foo` (`Executing genrule //foo:foo`) and leaves `//foo:bar` (`Executing genrule //foo:bar` absent) on `//foo:all`. Zel rechecks every action output, so an unlisted deleted or changed output is re-executed as well.

With `keep_going` true, every independent action still starts; `Crash.Code.CRASH_UNKNOWN` and `This is a catastrophe` are never produced. `--nokeep_going` does stop the ready queue after the first ordinary failure, and in-flight workers still finish (`thread::scope` joins them).
  - [P2] `testUpdateCacheError` stats `.../out/foo` successfully, then `getLastModifiedTime` and `getLastChangeTime` throw `IOException`. The build throws `BuildFailedException` and the reporter contains `not all outputs were created or valid` (the action failure after `checkOutputs` treats that `IOException` as a bad output; the per-output event is `output 'foo' was not created`). Zel `LocalFileSystem::stat` turns a failed `modified()` into mtime `0` and returns `Ok`. The action is cached and succeeds, so that string is not emitted. Zel uses `not all outputs were created or valid` only when an output is missing or a declared file is a directory: `ERROR: {loc}: {progress} failed: not all outputs were created or valid` for a spawn, or `ERROR: {loc}: {mnemonic} failed: not all outputs were created or valid` otherwise.
  - [P2] `testProgressReporting` records `EventKind.START` and `FINISH` only. With the test progress supplier returning `""`, each message is a leading space plus `Test ` plus the root-relative output name. The first build of `baz` must contain ` Test foo START`, ` Test foo FINISH`, ` Test bar START`, ` Test bar FINISH`, ` Test baz START`, ` Test baz FINISH` (`foo` has the 10 source inputs `file0`..`file9`, then `bar` depends on `foo`, `baz` on `bar`). After deleting `bar` and `baz`, the rebuild must contain only the `bar` and `baz` pairs. Zel never posts `EventKind.START` or `FINISH`. The UI progress text is the action's `progress_message`, or `{mnemonic} {owner}` when that is empty, and a cache hit still notifies action listeners.
  - [P2] `testReportsActionExecutedEvent` (`keep_going` true, one successful action) requires exactly one event-bus `ActionExecutedEvent` whose action is that action. Zel posts BEP `ActionExecuted` for a success only when BEP is on and `--build_event_publish_all_actions` is true (default `false`). Otherwise only a failed action is published, and only if an `ActionListener` is registered (`execute_actions` skips `action_started` / `action_finished` when there is none).
  - [P1] `testCyclicActionGraph`, `testSelfCyclicActionGraph`, `testCycleInActionGraphBelowTwoActions`, and `testCyclicActionGraphWithTail` each require `BuildFailedException` with message exactly `Yarrrr, there be a cycle up in here` (harness `execution.CYCLE`). The graphs are `foo→bar→baz→foo`; `foo→foo`; `foo1` and `foo2` both depending on `bar` while `bar↔baz`; and `bat` (no inputs) feeding `baz` while `foo→bar→baz→foo` (`baz` also depends on `bat`). Zel's header is `ERROR: cycle in the action graph:` and each following line is four spaces plus the stuck action's first output exec path, in ascending action index. Stderr containing `cycle` is classified as `analysis.CYCLE` (exit 1). A self-edge is dropped (`p == i`), so `foo→foo` is ready, `ScheduleResult.cycle` stays empty, and that build is not failed as a cycle. Dependents waiting on the cycle (`foo1`, `foo2`) are included in the stuck list with `bar` and `baz`.

Posted lost-input count is `2`. A nondeterministic `$$RANDOM` genrule is re-executed so the second bytes differ. Zel’s action cache keeps the first output.
  - [P2] The same lost input may be seen `20` times (`ActionRewindStrategy.MAX_REPEATED_LOST_INPUTS`). The 21st failure is `ActionRewinding.Code.LOST_INPUT_TOO_MANY_TIMES`, a bug report, and a message containing `lost input too many times (#21) for the same action. lostInput: {input}, lostInput digest: fakedigest/10, failedAction: action 'Executing genrule //test:rule2'`. Spawns repeat the pair 21 times and `//test:rule1` is rewound 20 times. Zel stores `experimental_max_repeated_lost_inputs` default `20` and never reads it. `MAX_ACTION_REWIND_EVENTS` is `5`. Six consume targets post a total lost-input count of `21` and keep only the five rewind samples with the most invalidated nodes. The profiler task `prepare action rewind plan` is unused; Bazel profiles `Preparing rewind plan for %d lost inputs of %s` and `Preparing rewind plan for %d lost outputs of %s`.
  - [P2] An interrupt on the rewound `//test:rule1` stops with `InterruptedException`. A rewound action that exits 1 (`Spawn.Code.NON_ZERO_EXIT`, runner `remote`, exception text `kaboom`) fails with `Executing genrule //test:rule1 failed: (Exit 1)`. Under keep-going the `BuildFailedException` message is null; under `--nokeep_going` it contains that string. Zel has no `ActionRewoundEvent`. Parallel shared actions rewind each action index `0` once and the output is `hi i am a shared input\nhi i am a shared input\n`. Zel does not coalesce `ActionExecutionState` or reset the sibling waiting on that future.
  - [P2] A directly depended `TreeFileArtifact` `make_cc_dir.cc/file1.cc` rewinds only `//tree:make_cc` action index `0`. One or all of the `.pic.o` children rewinds both compile actions, then the tree artifact. With `--experimental_allow_map_directory`, a rewound expansion must observe zero readers (`the rewound action template expansion prepared for its re-execution while consumers were still reading the tree artifact it populates`). One lost generated runfile still rewinds both `//middle:gen1` and `//middle:gen2`. A lost input that is both a direct tool and a runfile invalidates `//test:rule1` before the runfiles nodes. Three outputs of one genrule split across depset children rewind `//test:gen` once.
  - [P2] A generated header lost in input discovery or in `Compiling genheader/consumes.cc` rewinds only `//genheader:gen_header`. When `AnalysisMock` is Bazel, expected spawn lists drop descriptions that start with `Extracting include lines `. A lost `dep.pic.pcm` rewinds that artifact and runs `Compiling foo/dep.cppmap` twice. `BUILDING_PARENT_FOUND_UNDONE_CHILD` with no prior rewind throws `IllegalStateException` containing `Unexpected undone children`. If `//foo:flaky_lost` fails on the rewound attempt, keep-going posts `TargetCompleteEvent`s for both tops whose root cause is `//foo:flaky_lost`; `--nokeep_going` posts exactly one. Two lost inputs with the same contents rewind both deps and post one `ActionRewoundEvent`.
  - [P2] With `--norewind_lost_inputs`, a lost top-level output `bin/foo/gen.out` fails with `ActionRewinding.Code.LOST_OUTPUT_REWINDING_DISABLED` and `//foo:gen: Unexpected lost outputs (pass --rewind_lost_inputs to enable recovery): foo/gen.out`. Zel never emits `Unexpected lost outputs`. With rewinding on, only the lost output is rebuilt (`Action foo/lost.out` twice, `Action foo/found.out` once). An aspect output rewinds an `AspectKey`. A lost tree file rewinds the generating action first and then the tree artifact. Completion events are withheld until after rewind. Under `--nokeep_going`, a failed sibling prevents output rewinding. A top-level output lost `21` times fails with `LOST_OUTPUT_TOO_MANY_TIMES` and `Lost output foo/lost.out (digest {hex}/{size}), and rewinding was ineffective after 20 attempts.` The digest is lowercase hex, a `/`, then the byte size. The lost-output count is `21`.

  - [P3] The parent directory is the substring before the last `/`. `/`, the empty string, and a name with no slash all yield an empty parent, which is the listing key.

### `src/test/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/skyframe/serialization/testutils/IsomorphismKeyTest.java`
- Bazel lines: 113
- Zel counterpart: `none`
- Verdict: missing
- Differences:
  - [P3] Zel has no isomorphism-key graph and no joint depth-first equality over fingerprint-labeled nodes with ordered, possibly cyclic links.
  - [P3] Same fingerprint and no links must compare equal; different fingerprints must compare unequal.
  - [P3] Matching self-cycles must compare equal: a node already seen on both sides is equal, and a visit-new mismatch is unequal.
  - [P3] A self-link versus no links must compare unequal.
  - [P3] A diamond (`a` to `b` and `c`, both to one shared `d`) must compare equal when fingerprints and link order match.
  - [P3] The same shape with two distinct `d` nodes that share a fingerprint must compare unequal, because sharing is by node identity, not by fingerprint.

Keys are `//pkg1:main_target` with `foo = default`, and `//pkg1:dep_1` twice, with `foo = v1` and `foo = v2`. Zel has no attr-aspects function that sees that unconfigured label, and it does not key aspect applications by the full configuration option value.

Searches under `/workspace/zel-cursor/crates` for `TestRunnableWrapper`, `ThrowableRecordingRunnableWrapper`, `waitForTasksAndMaybeThrow`, and `getFirstThrownError` found no match. `/workspace/zel-cursor/crates/zel-skyframe/src/engine.rs` catches panics inside Skyframe evaluation, which is a different control path.
  - [P3] The constructor forwards `name` to `ThrowableRecordingRunnableWrapper`. A null name throws `NullPointerException` before the wrapper exists. `name` is used only when a task fails: the worker logs severe `"Error thrown by runnable in %s"` with that throwable as the cause. The first failure is stored with `compareAndSet(null, error)`; later failures are logged and discarded. `getFirstThrownError` returns that stored throwable, or null.
  - [P3] `wrap` delegates to that recorder, then returns a runnable that increments an `AtomicInteger` before the delegate runs and decrements it in `finally`. The delegate swallows every `Throwable`, including `Error`, so the outer `run` does not propagate the task failure. The count changes only once `run` has been entered, so a wrapper that is queued but not started stays at zero. Wrapping an already wrapped runnable nests another increment and decrement.
  - [P3] `waitForTasksAndMaybeThrow` is a `do`/`while` that reads the stored failure before sleeping. A stored `Error` or `RuntimeException` is rethrown unchanged (`Throwables.propagateIfPossible`). Any other `Throwable` is thrown as `new RuntimeException(cause)`, so a checked exception such as `InterruptedException` is wrapped and the message is `cause.toString()`. That throw happens even when the count is still above zero; other wrappers are left running and are not interrupted.
  - [P3] If nothing is stored, the call always `Thread.sleep(100)` before testing the count, including when the count is already zero, then repeats while the count is `> 0`. Completion is not signaled, so a failure that occurs during the sleep is observed only on the next iteration, and a count that falls to zero is noticed only after the current sleep. `InterruptedException` from `sleep` propagates from the wait itself and clears the interrupt status; it is not stored as a task failure.

### `src/test/java/com/google/devtools/build/skyframe/TrackingAwaiter.java`
- Bazel lines: 95
- Zel counterpart: `none`
- Verdict: missing
- Differences:
  - [P3] The only instance is the public static `INSTANCE`. A private constructor blocks any other instance. It keeps one process-wide `ConcurrentLinkedQueue` of `(message, throwable)` pairs. `awaitLatchAndTrackExceptions` is the only method that both records and rethrows. `injectExceptionAndMessage` only enqueues. Zel has no shared test-failure queue, no `INSTANCE`, and no later assertion over swallowed thread-pool exceptions.
  - [P3] `waitAndMaybeThrowInterrupt` calls `Uninterruptibles.awaitUninterruptibly(latch, TestUtils.WAIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, SECONDS)` with `WAIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = Long.MAX_VALUE / 1000`. `TimeUnit.SECONDS.toNanos` saturates that to `Long.MAX_VALUE` nanoseconds (about 292 years). Guava’s `end = System.nanoTime() + remaining` then overflows a signed long, so an interrupt while the count is still above zero makes the retry timeout negative, `CountDownLatch.await` returns false at once, `Thread.interrupted()` clears the flag, and the method throws `InterruptedException` with a null message. A latch that reaches zero returns successfully and leaves the interrupt status set, including when this thread was already interrupted before `await` (the race `CountDownLatch.await` would turn into an immediate `InterruptedException` without reading the count). If the saturated wait ends with the flag clear, it throws `AssertionError` whose message is the caller’s `errorMessage`. `awaitLatchAndTrackExceptions` stores that original throwable with `errorMessage`, then `Throwables.propagate`: `AssertionError` and other unchecked throwables are rethrown as themselves, and `InterruptedException` is wrapped in a new `RuntimeException` whose cause is the stored exception. Zel has no uninterruptible test latch wait, no `Long.MAX_VALUE / 1000` timeout, and no those two failure types. The `Condvar` in `/workspace/zel-cursor/crates/zel-skyframe/src/engine.rs` only parks idle or dependency-blocked workers for 20ms.
  - [P3] `assertNoErrors` copies the queue, then `clear`s it, then Truth-asserts that the copy is empty. The copy is FIFO. A failure therefore drops the recorded pairs from the queue, and a pair added between the copy and the clear is discarded and never asserted. The stored throwables are not rethrown or attached as causes. `injectExceptionAndMessage` can plant a pair that fails this assertion without throwing at the inject call. Zel has no snapshot-and-clear test assertion of this queue.

Unannotated lambdas run, because no call is type-checked.

The whole input must be exactly one string token: `'hello'`, `"hello"`, and `r'a\b"c'` return the decoded value (`a\b"c` for the raw literal). Empty input, surrounding spaces, identifiers, and numbers throw `IllegalArgumentException` containing `invalid syntax`. An unclosed quote throws with `unclosed string literal`, and `'\g'` throws with `invalid escape sequence: \g. Use '\\' to insert '\'.`.

A mismatched unindent aborts with `unindent does not match any outer indentation level` instead of `indentation error` plus `OUTDENT`. A tab is an 8-column indent and does not report `Tab characters are not allowed for indentation. Use spaces instead.`. Invalid characters, unclosed strings, and a backslash that is not a line continuation abort the scan instead of skipping the character or emitting `ILLEGAL` and continuing. `012345` is decimal 12345, not value 0 with `invalid octal literal: 012345 (use '0o12345')`. `0o` and `0or()` abort instead of `INT(0)` plus `invalid base-8 integer literal`. `0o12349` is split into a valid octal and a following number, not one `INT(0)` with `invalid base-8 integer literal: 0o12349`. `1e` and `1e+x` abort with `exponent has no digits` instead of `FLOAT(0.0)` and `invalid float literal`. `1.0e309` is infinity with no `floating-point literal too large`. `...`, `....`, and `1....1` are dots, not `ELLIPSIS`. `\u` is read as a hex escape instead of `invalid escape sequence: \u` with value `ab\ucd`. Octal `\777` and `\401` are not reported as out of range and are not masked to `0xff`. `\8` keeps the same characters but omits `invalid escape sequence: \8`. A backslash plus CRLF in a string is not a line continuation: raw strings keep the CR, and quoted strings can be reported unclosed instead of `STRING(ab)`.

Leading spaces and indentation are stripped, a blank line or a plain `#` ends the block, a trailing `#:` overrides a leading one and applies only to the last statement on that line, and `#:` inside a string is not a doc comment. The execution lexer drops `#` through the end of the line. `/workspace/zel-cursor/crates/zel-starlark/src/syntax/bazel_syntax.rs` does not record doc comments, and no statement carries one.
